intro: Before/after shapes of the work — what changed when the harness showed up.

cases.title: From brief to reviewable spike
cases.before: A crisp UI/tool idea waited for “a free weekend” and often never shipped.
cases.after: Same brief becomes a public or internal spike in hours to a day, with an engineer still owning taste and production readiness.
harness: Human gate before any public claim
cases.lesson: Agents collapse blank-page cost. They do not replace product judgment.

cases.title: Agentic work in a real codebase
cases.before: Copy-paste between chat and editor; context lost every session.
cases.after: Cockpit reads the tree, patches, runs tests, opens reviewable diffs; human steers and merges.
cases.lesson: The unit of progress is a reviewable change with proof — not a confident paragraph.

cases.title: Human-in-the-loop target investigation
cases.before: One engineer serial-debugs alone; notes live in a notebook that the next session cannot load.
cases.after: Agent runs bounded commands; human judges logs and hardware reality; failures become skills.
cases.lesson: Power without proof class becomes expensive fiction.

cases.title: Team-shaped solo bursts
cases.before: One chat tries to own design, docs, and implementation; thrash increases.
cases.after: Named lanes with owns/never/handoffs; humans still approve binding decisions.
cases.lesson: Parallelism is a multiplier only when ownership is explicit.

cases.title: Behaviour as a versioned product
cases.before: Good habits died when the chat ended; every new session relearned pain.
cases.after: Skills, rules, and signed patterns live in version control and compound for months.
cases.lesson: This is the compounding advantage — quieter than demos, larger over time.

cases.title: Guarded operational assistance
cases.before: Manual drafts and risky “just send it” moments.
cases.after: Assistants draft freely; irreversible outbound requires a human gate with the full referent visible.
cases.lesson: Draft freely; irreversible outbound still needs a visible human gate.

cases.title: Runtime policy + model routing
cases.before: Tool use unaudited beyond chat discipline; single-upstream model lock-in.
cases.after: Preloop layered under P0 for tool audit/policy; OpenRouter for multi-model routing with vaulted keys.
cases.lesson: Runtime and routing support the harness — they do not replace human consent or proof class.

cases.title: WhatsApp triage without autonomy cosplay
cases.before: Either ignore the channel or risk eager auto-replies to the wrong person.
cases.after: Briar-style monitor/triage: one watcher, light carve-outs, drafts elsewhere, voice as a medium with the same gates.
cases.lesson: A messaging assistant is a harness surface with the same fail-closed rules as the cockpit.

cases.title: Token lean as operating discipline
cases.before: Always-on essays and idle tool catalogs made every turn expensive before work started.
cases.after: Thin skills, requestable rules, lean MCP sessions, and measured always-on budgets keep the cockpit fast.
cases.lesson: Optimising tokens is how the working relationship stays affordable — not stinginess.

cases.title: Specs stay in git; exports are views
cases.before: Branded DOCX copies drifted; comments never returned to the canonical text.
cases.after: Markdown SoT in git; branded DOCX/PDF and Drive mirrors for humans; comment ingest back to SoT.
cases.lesson: One source of truth; many views.
